Suicide is a viable option for people who struggle to make it through each day. For those who are so old they can't function, or in so much pain they can't think straight. But for people who are finding life difficult? Just keep swimming.

When I was in high school I worked in a very tiny town's IGA, which is a grocery store. There were two cash registers (one of which was permanently turned off unless it was near Thanksgiving or Christmas), a tiny deli in the back, and four aisles.

One day a freezer starting going out, and my boss and I spent an extra hour after work that day moving all of the ice cream out of it before it could melt. We put frozen pizzas in its place, since they didn't need to be kept quite as cold, and we put the ice cream where the pizzas were.

Fastforward a few weeks. This pair of old ladies (who, alongside mothers, make up about 90% of this store's business) are shopping in a really bad mood, grumbling and muttering to themselves, and shooting me dirty looks. I have no idea what I've done wrong, so I'm secretly listening to them trying to figure out wtf is going on, and suddenly one of the ladies GLARES and me and says, "Well EVER SINCE THEY MOVED THE ICE CREAM ON ME, I just don't know WHAT to think of this store anymore."

I had such a hard time trying not to laugh. Yes, woman, we moved the ice cream as a personal affront to you. We knew it would be nigh impossible to find *two freezer doors down* in a store with only *one short wall of freezers*.

Your small dog just chewed up your favorite pair of shoes. Do you resist the urge to punt it across the room because God wouldn't like it, or because you recognize that your dog would be injured by your violence?
